Qualify source-intervention transport and bounded capture cost
Seal an available tool-grounding corpus and independent roles

summary: Milestone 2026.09.659 completed 4 experiments, all compute-bound, in 41.3 wall-time minutes. The dominant task was 'Bind fourteen tasks and ingest source-grounding methods' at 34.6 minutes, followed by 'Qualify source-intervention transport and bounded capture cost' at 5.47 minutes, with the remaining two tasks taking 1.05 minutes and 0.21 minutes. Sub-phase timing was not recorded within these runs to separate model inference execution from evaluation scaffolding or artifact serialization overhead.
bottlenecks_identified: 'Bind fourteen tasks and ingest source-grounding methods' accounted for 34.6 out of 41.3 total wall-time minutes (approx. 84% of milestone execution time), but lacks granular sub-phase instrumentation to isolate model execution from evaluation scaffolding or artifact serialization.

'Qualify source-intervention transport and bounded capture cost' consumed 5.47 minutes without recorded internal stage durations, leaving the distribution between model inference, transport validation, and file I/O unmeasured.

The remaining two compute-bound tasks completed rapidly (tool-grounding corpus sealing at 1.05 minutes and conjugate energy memory building at 0.21 minutes), with timestamps reconstructed from disk mtimes rather than continuous runtime stage logs.

The GPU monitor report provides an isolated snapshot (GPU 0 at 0% utilization with 18064MB allocated, GPU 1 at 97% utilization with 18866MB allocated) at milestone end, leaving GPU utilization and active memory bandwidth across individual compute task execution windows unmeasured.
Task launch records did not log model concurrency or runner dispatch receipts, though all completed tasks were single-model executions where DualGPURunner multi-model dispatch is not applicable.
improvements_suggested: Instrument granular sub-phase duration timers and monotonic stage logging inside task binding and source-intervention transport workflows to isolate model inference latency from evaluation scaffolding and disk serialization.

Deploy continuous, task-aligned accelerator telemetry during compute-bound executions to sample live GPU utilization and VRAM occupancy across active compute windows rather than relying on point-in-time monitor snapshots.
Implement batched inference across evaluation loops (e.g. batching 8-16 questions per forward pass as suggested in monitor telemetry) to improve throughput on single-process model workloads.
Emit explicit model concurrency and runner dispatch metadata in experiment task receipts to audit DualGPURunner eligibility whenever two or more models run concurrently.
Implement runtime milestone-scoped execution logging to avoid reliance on post-hoc disk-mtime timing reconstruction.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Instrument sub-phase duration timers and per-stage progress logging inside the task binding and source-intervention transport pipelines.
Deploy continuous accelerator telemetry during compute-bound task execution to record live GPU utilization and VRAM occupancy across active execution windows.
Implement batched inference (batching 8-16 questions per forward pass) for single-process evaluation workflows to increase GPU throughput.
meta_reflection: The milestone completed 4 compute-bound tasks in 41.3 wall-time minutes, heavily concentrated in task binding and source-grounding ingestion (34.6 minutes) and source-intervention qualification (5.47 minutes). The end-state GPU monitor report confirms active compute on GPU 1 (97% utilization) but cannot evaluate active-window efficiency across individual task spans, and because only single-model tasks ran, no DualGPURunner opportunity was missed. Sub-phase timing and continuous execution telemetry are necessary next steps to identify actionable latency optimizations.
